title: Transactional Temporal Indicator History Ownership & Commit Composition
goal: Qualify the transaction-owned lifecycle of the previous accepted right-derivative history required by F-SI25, including warmup, trial isolation, accepted-substep advancement, retry, rollback, checkpoint and external commit semantics, without selecting a scientific tolerance or admitting the Richards indicator as a production acceptance certificate.
problem_statement: F-SI25 needs the right derivative from the immediately preceding accepted state transition.
F-SI25 deliberately does not own persistent history.
A worker/model-local history cache is invalid because columns, retries and A-B-A ordering can reuse workers.
A post-external-commit side variable is insufficient because F-KT09 can accept multiple private substeps inside one requested external interval.
The history must therefore follow the same accepted-trial clone/rollback semantics as the canonical state while remaining explicitly categorized as numerical continuation, not physical water state.

candidates.name: worker_or_solver_local_history
candidates.reason: Not column-lineage-owned; unsafe under retries, worker reuse and MultiSWAP A-B-A execution.

candidates.name: post_external_commit_runtime_side_variable
candidates.reason: Cannot correctly advance between privately accepted F-KT09 substeps and risks postcommit split ownership.

candidates.name: generic_kernel_committed_sidecar_outside_inner_transaction_state
candidates.reason: Atomic external commit can be made safe, but inner canonical substep acceptance would require a second transaction mechanism or invasive API plumbing.

candidates.name: feature_scoped_numerical_continuation_subobject_cloned_with_transaction_state
candidates.reason: Attempt clones naturally isolate history; accepted private substeps naturally advance it; retries discard trial mutations; no separate publication authority is introduced. Physical and numerical-continuation fields must remain logically explicit and separately typed.

selection_requirements: No worker-local or global hidden ownership.
No numerical-continuation field is interpreted as physical water storage or enters MassLedger/storage accounting.
Inactive columns allocate no derivative vector.
A checkpoint clone captures the exact continuation history associated with its physical origin revision.
A candidate carries history from its accepted private substep path, not from rejected trials.
External commit remains the existing F-KT move/publication boundary.
No HeadCalc-private arrays become transaction state.

candidate_history_semantics.availability: explicit logical/allocated state; unavailable at initial warmup unless a qualified restart supplies matching history
candidate_history_semantics.payload: right derivative vector associated with the immediately preceding accepted soil-water substep
candidate_history_semantics.dimension: active soil-water nodes for the model-specific continuation payload
candidate_history_semantics.origin: the exact accepted transition that produced the current committed/substep state
candidate_history_semantics.trial_read: read from the cloned origin transaction state
candidate_history_semantics.trial_candidate: F-SI25 current_right_derivative from a converged admitted solve
candidate_history_semantics.accepted_private_substep: replace the clone's history with the accepted candidate derivative before it becomes the next canonical working state
candidate_history_semantics.rejected_trial: discard derivative candidate with the rejected trial clone
candidate_history_semantics.retry: restart from unchanged accepted origin history
candidate_history_semantics.external_candidate: contains the continuation history resulting from all privately accepted substeps up to requested t1
candidate_history_semantics.external_commit: publishes physical and continuation state together through the existing F-KT candidate commit
candidate_history_semantics.restart: history is optional numerical continuation state; if claimed present it must be checkpoint/restart-consistent with the physical lineage/time, otherwise unavailable/fail closed

F_SI25_composition.call_point: after a converged admitted reference-Richards solve and before trial state publication within the model advance
F_SI25_composition.warmup: if previous derivative unavailable, do not claim B_inf available; still retain current derivative if the physical trial is accepted
F_SI25_composition.reason_certificate_not_populated: F-KT09 requires a finite nonnegative dimensionless indicator <= 1, while F-SI25 deliberately provides an unnormalized head-domain indicator and no scientific temporal limit has been selected.

gates.A_architecture_selection: Persist candidate comparison and select only a design satisfying transaction atomicity, explicit data separation and optional-state scaling.
gates.B_continuation_carrier: Implement the selected separately typed feature-scoped numerical continuation carrier with exact clone semantics and no mass-accounting participation.
gates.C_trial_retry_rollback: Prove rejected solver/temporal/mass trials and retries cannot mutate accepted history; accepted private substeps advance it exactly once.
gates.D_checkpoint_external_commit: Prove checkpoint reuse preserves origin history and external candidate commit/rollback publishes or discards physical+continuation state atomically.
gates.E_F_SI25_binding: Bind F-SI25 history input/current derivative output in the admitted reference-Richards envelope without changing its formula, operator policy, cost or physical result.
gates.F_feature_scoped_MultiSWAP: Prove inactive columns carry no vector state and A-B-A/multi-column execution has no cross-column leakage.
gates.G_owner_replay: Replay F-SI25 exact-linear, owner and frozen F-VQ30 production cases through transaction-supplied history where applicable; numerical outputs and hard mass remain identical.
gates.H_compiler_identity: O0/O2 identity for focused transaction/history qualification.

hard_holds: No scientific temporal tolerance or normalization is selected.
Do not set trial_outcome temporal_certificate_available from B_inf in F-KT10.
Do not turn B_inf into a <=1 acceptance decision.
Do not claim B_inf is a general nonlinear true-error upper bound.
Do not add q_cap, Nmin, geometric-tail multipliers, fitted factors or deep refinement trajectories.
Do not change F-KT09 default full-vs-two-half behavior or generic certificate semantics.
Do not change Richards physics, forcing, boundary semantics or mass accounting.
Do not count numerical continuation history as water storage or MassLedger mass.
Do not store history for inactive columns.
Do not move commit authority outside F-KT.
Do not release F-GC02, groundwater coupling or F-PE.
